title: Direct Sums Reconstruct Supercuspidal Data
body_html:
Direct Sums Reconstruct Supercuspidal Data

Let \(\Sigma_l\) be single-block supercuspidal data with one depth-zero block and positive-depth blocks of pairwise distinct depths. Their direct sum \[ \Sigma=\bigoplus_l \Sigma_l \] is a supercuspidal datum. Moreover, direct sum reconstruction is inverse to block decomposition on equivalence classes of data.
proof_html:
Take the orthogonal direct sum of the underlying hermitian spaces and define \(x\), \(\Gamma\), and \(\phi\) componentwise. Since the positive depths are pairwise distinct, the Moy-Prasad filtration separates the summands: no off-diagonal term has the same leading depth as two different blocks. The centralizer of \(\Gamma\) is therefore the product of the block centralizers.

The finite reductive quotient representation is the exterior tensor product of the quotient representations on the blocks. The defining Yu-data conditions are checked block by block: the positive-depth blocks supply the required good elements at their depths, and the block \(\Sigma_0\) supplies the depth-zero cuspidal representation.

Applying block decomposition to the direct sum recovers the original blocks, because the depths and the primitive idempotents of \(F^0[\Gamma]\) are exactly the ones used to form the sum. Thus direct sum reconstruction is inverse to block decomposition on equivalence classes.
